entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer
entries.description:
Use a mouse and keyboard to interact with a web browser, and take screenshots. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.
* Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element before moving the cursor.
* If you tried clicking on a program or link but it failed to load, even after waiting, try adjusting your click location so that the tip of the cursor visually falls on the element that you want to click.
* Make sure to click any buttons, links, icons, etc with the cursor tip in the center of the element. Don't click boxes on their edges unless asked.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported and will return an error - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels. Requires a Claude in Chrome extension version that supports scale; older extensions return the full-size image.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

tabId.description: Tab ID to execute the action on. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

save_to_disk.description: For screenshot/zoom actions: save the image to disk so it can be attached to a message for the user. Returns the saved path in the tool result. Only set this when you intend to share the image — screenshots you're just looking at don't need saving.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

# v1 → v2 efficiency: victim runs per bisect (fixture, $0)

Generated by `uv run python scripts/v2_efficiency.py` on 2026-10-10 (branch `feat/v2-efficiency`). The
fixture victim has no LLM: 10 tasks, k = 3, five "fragile" tasks that drop from 0.95 to 0.05 at the
planted commit. Every run below named the planted commit. The numbers are deterministic; a re-run
printed the same table.

What changed in v2:

- **Staged baseline** (`culprit/baseline.py`). Screen every task ×1 on both ends, then run the full k
  only on tasks that did not pass on both ends. Both ends run the same (task, repetition) set, and the
  Fisher gate uses the runs that were actually made.
- **Baseline reuse** (`culprit/reuse.py`). Results at a commit are copied from an earlier run that matches
  on commit SHA, suite SHA, victim provider and model, eval module and k. Each copied row records its
  source run (`reused_from_run`, `reused_from_id`) and is not counted as spend again.

Bisect runs are the same in v1 and v2 on every scenario: the cheaper baseline didn't make the bisect
any harder.

EOF
cat $T
cat <<'EOF'

## What this means on the real victim (projection, not measured)

Run `ff50e3620fdd` (v1, `hist/b`, GLM 5.3) made 240 victim runs: 156 baseline + 84 bisect, $0.60.
Its good end was 78/78, and 7 tasks dropped on the bad end. The v2 screen would be 26 + 26 = 52 runs.
Assuming those 7 tasks fail the screen on the bad end, they get the full k: 7 × 2 more reps × 2 ends = 28.
That makes the baseline about **80 runs instead of 156**, and the whole bisect about **164 runs instead of
240 (−32%)**. A second branch from `good-v1.0` with the same suite, model and k would also reuse the good
end (about 40 runs), so it would need about 124 runs (−48%). These numbers will be confirmed by a real v2
run. The fixture's 50% fragile tasks overstate the full-k share compared with RefundDesk's 7 of 26.
EOF
} > evidence/v2-efficiency-fixture.md && mkdir -p business

# cfo.ai inputs: Culprit unit economics and pricing hypotheses

Written 2026-10-10. This file gathers the numbers to type into cfo.ai by hand. Every figure is
marked **measured** (from a run's ledger or the build log), **projected** (derived from measured
numbers with a stated assumption) or **assumption**. Pricing scenarios A, B and C are
**hypotheses**: no customer has seen or validated any of them.

To refresh the measured inputs from the ledger:

```bash
uv run culprit export-costs --format csv --out business/runs.csv   # per run: cost, victim runs, wall time
```

## 1. Measured

| Input | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Real bisect, `hist/b`, GLM 5.3 victim (v1) | 240 victim runs, **$0.60**, 12.5 min | run `ff50e3620fdd` (hackathon.md) |
| … of which baseline / bisect | 156 / 84 runs | same run |
| Cost per victim run, GLM 5.3 | $0.0025 | $0.60 / 240 |
| Cost per victim run, Claude Sonnet 5.5 | $0.0163 | RefundDesk baseline, 78 runs for $1.27, at $2/$10 per MTok |
| Culprit's own LLM cost per bisect | $0 | no Culprit LLM stage runs in `culprit run` yet |
| v1 → v2 victim runs per bisect, fixture | −16% (staging alone), −34% (good end reused), −47% (both ends reused) | `evidence/v2-efficiency-fixture.md` |

## 2. Projected (cost of goods per bisect)

The v2 run counts are a projection for `hist/b` (see `evidence/v2-efficiency-fixture.md`): 164 runs
with a staged baseline, 124 when the good end is reused. Compute is an **assumption** of $0.04 per
bisect: one 4-vCPU runner at about $0.17/hour for about 12.5 minutes.

| Victim model | v1 (240 runs) | v2 (164 runs) | v2 + good reused (124 runs) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Claude Sonnet 5.5 | $3.95 | $2.71 | $2.06 |
| GLM 5.3 | $0.64 | $0.45 | $0.35 |

These include the $0.04 compute. They exclude fixed costs (hosting, neatlogs plan, support), which
cfo.ai should take as separate monthly lines; we have no measured values for them.

## 3. Pricing scenarios (hypotheses)

Bisects per repo per month is unknown. The tables use 10 and 30 as **assumptions**.

### A. Flat subscription per repo, Culprit pays the model

- Starter: **$49/repo/month**, 10 bisects included.
- Team: **$199/repo/month**, 30 bisects included.

| Plan | Model | COGS / month | Gross margin |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Starter (10) | Sonnet, v1 | $39.48 | 19% |
| Starter (10) | Sonnet, v2 | $27.10 | 45% |
| Starter (10) | GLM, v2 | $4.50 | 91% |
| Team (30) | Sonnet, v1 | $118.43 | 40% |
| Team (30) | Sonnet, v2 | $81.31 | 59% |
| Team (30) | GLM, v2 | $13.50 | 93% |

Risk: margin depends on the customer's victim model and on usage. A cap on included bisects is needed.

### B. Bring your own key, plus a platform fee

The customer's own model key pays for victim runs (about $2.67 per bisect on Sonnet 5.5, v2). Culprit charges
**$99/repo/month**.

| Bisects / month | Culprit COGS (compute only) | Gross margin |
|---|---:|---:|
| 10 | $0.40 | 99.6% |
| 30 | $1.20 | 98.8% |
| 100 | $4.00 | 96.0% |

Risk: there's no model-cost exposure, but the customer sees two bills. v2's efficiency lowers *their*
bill, not ours.

### C. Metered per bisect, Culprit pays the model

Charge **$5 per completed bisect**. A run that ends as `no_regression` or `budget_exceeded` costs less,
and charging for it is an open question.

| Model / version | COGS per bisect | Gross margin at $5 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Sonnet 5.5, v1 | $3.95 | 21% |
| Sonnet 5.5, v2 | $2.71 | 46% |
| GLM 5.3, v1 | $0.64 | 87% |
| GLM 5.3, v2 | $0.45 | 91% |

This is the scenario where v2's efficiency matters most: on Sonnet it roughly doubles the margin
(21% → 46%).

## 4. Still to measure

- A real v2 run on `hist/b`, to replace the projected 164 runs with a measured number.
- The other five branches (`hist/a`, `c`–`f`), to get an average bisect cost rather than one run.
- Runs per bisect with Culprit's own LLM stages (localiser, fixer, verifier) once they're built.
- Fixed monthly costs and the expected bisects per repo per month. Both are needed before cfo.ai's
  runway and break-even figures mean anything.

content.text:
Both tasks are finished and committed as `69e6b60` on `feat/v2-efficiency` in the `piedpiper-neathacks-v2` worktree. All 85 tests pass (17 are new). Nothing was pushed, no paid runs were made, and the main folder and RefundDesk weren't touched.

## Task 1: v1 → v2 efficiency

- **Staged baseline** (`culprit/baseline.py`): every task runs once on both ends. Only tasks that didn't pass on both ends get the rest of k. Both ends always run the same set of runs, and the Fisher gate counts the runs actually made (a test checks this).
- **Baseline reuse** (`culprit/reuse.py`): results are copied from an earlier run with the same commit SHA, suite SHA, victim provider and model, eval module and k. Each copied row records the run and row it came from. Copied runs aren't charged again, so the budget caps and totals stay correct.
- **Before/after on the fixture** (`scripts/v2_efficiency.py`, `evidence/v2-efficiency-fixture.md`), victim runs over 4 scenarios:

  | Version | Victim runs | Change vs v1 |
  |---|---:|---:|
  | v1 | 510 | |
  | v2, staged baseline | 430 | −16% |
  | v2, good end reused | 335 | −34% |
  | v2, both ends reused | 270 | −47% |

  All 16 runs found the planted commit, and the bisect steps used the same number of runs in v1 and v2.
- **Real victim (projection only, not measured):** `hist/b` would need about 164 victim runs instead of 240.

## Task 2: M6

- **`culprit report <run_id>`** (`report.py`) writes markdown and a static HTML page. It shows the verdict, the bisect timeline with Wilson intervals against the threshold, skips, intent, diff, trace IDs, costs, and where any reused results came from. I checked the HTML in a browser.
- **`culprit export-costs --format csv`** (`costs.py`) gives per-run cost, victim runs (executed, baseline, bisect, reused) and wall time.
- **`business/cfo-inputs.md`** separates measured, projected and assumed numbers, and labels pricing scenarios A, B and C as hypotheses.

# Culprit

`git bisect` for agent behaviour, with receipts.

Give Culprit a good ref, a bad ref and an eval suite. It finds the commit that broke your agent, explains why that change was made (from the Entire session), proposes the smallest fix that restores quality while keeping the intended gain, and verifies it statistically.

Team PiedPiper, neatHack 2026. Work in progress: see `PRD.md` for the spec and `hackathon.md` for the build log.

## Status

Bootstrap complete. Culprit build (M1) starts next.

## Docs

- `docs/research.md`: what the neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai docs actually support
- `docs/neatlogs.md`: tracing contract, coverage, and how to repeat the readback evidence loop
# Run register

Every paid run against the real victim (RefundDesk), plus the free checks that back a claim. Numbers come from the Culprit ledger (`.culprit/ledger.sqlite`) or from the check's own log, never estimates. Costs use our price table (GLM 5.3 via OpenRouter: $0.039/$4.80 per MTok), not neatlogs' figures (see `BLOCKERS.md`).

- **Culprit traces** (workflow `culprit`): the neatlogs session ID is the run ID.
- **Victim traces** (workflow `refunddesk-eval`): tagged with `culprit_run_id`, `commit_sha`, `task_id` and `repetition`.

## 9. Victim agent and seeded benchmark

### 9.1 Victim agent: "RefundDesk"
A customer-support agent that resolves refund requests using **mock tools** backed by a local JSON store:
`lookup_order`, `get_refund_policy`, `issue_refund`, `escalate_to_human`, `send_customer_email`.
The mock layer can inject failures (timeouts, `status: failed` payloads) deterministically per task seed.

**Eval suite:** 20 tasks + 6 held-out tasks. Each task = customer message + initial store state + **deterministic checker** on the final store state and tool-call log (e.g. "refund issued exactly once for ≤ $500", "escalated when order not found", "no refund when lookup failed").

### 9.2 Seeded regressions (ground truth)
Each scenario is a commit range of ~12–16 commits in the separate victim repo, with noise commits (docs, refactors, logging) around one culprit.

| ID | Culprit change | Intended gain | Symptom |
|---|---|---|---|
| **R1 (hero)** | "Make it faster": coding agent parallelises tool calls and **removes tool-result validation** | Lower latency | Refunds issued when `lookup_order` failed |
| R2 | Prompt cleanup drops the "> $500 needs escalation" rule | Shorter prompt / cost | Large refunds issued without escalation |
| R3 | Tool schema renames `order_id` → `id` without updating the description | API consistency | Wrong/missing arguments on lookup |
| R4 | `max_retries` 3 → 0 "to reduce latency" | Latency | Fails on flaky-tool tasks |
| R5 | Conversation history window shortened | Token cost | Loses customer details from earlier turns |
| R6 | Lenient JSON parsing of tool calls | Fewer parse errors | Malformed calls executed with defaults |

Plus **one uninstallable commit** (broken dependency pin) placed near the midpoint of at least two scenarios, to exercise skip recovery.

**Honesty rule:** The regressions are deliberately seeded. R1 is created through a real coding-agent session (captured by Entire) given the instruction "make it faster". We say this plainly in the demo and README.

## 10. Verification

A fix is **verified** only if all hold:
1. **Quality:** On full suite + held-out tasks × k, the Wilson interval for `bad+fix` overlaps or exceeds the `good` baseline interval.
2. **Intended gain kept:** The intent metric (latency / tokens / cost, taken from the commit intent) for `bad+fix` is no worse than `bad` by more than a configured tolerance.
3. **No new failures:** No task that passes on `good` fails consistently (all k) on `bad+fix`.

**Benchmark verification of Culprit itself** (`culprit bench`): for each of R1–R6, record whether the culprit commit was correct, whether the hunk was correct, whether the fix verified, victim runs used, cost, wall time. Ground truth is stored in `bench/ground_truth.json` in the Culprit repo (never in the victim repo). Victim history branches use neutral names (`hist/a`…`hist/f`); the scenario mapping lives only in the Culprit repo.

## 11. Failure handling and recovery
## 14. Required tools

### 14.1 neatlogs
- **Tracing:** every victim task run is a trace tagged `commit_sha`, `task_id`, `repetition`, `run_id`. Culprit's own LLM calls are traced separately.
- **Readback:** Task Selector and Localiser pull failing traces via the neatlogs CLI/Public API.
- **Detections:** regex rule on tool results containing `"status": "failed"` followed by `issue_refund`; condition rules such as `cost_usd > <cap>` for runaway runs.
- **Investigate:** used on Culprit **v1** benchmark runs to find why it misidentified or wasted runs.
- **Experiments (prompt versions):** Culprit's Localiser/Task Selector prompts versioned; v1 → v2 promoted by label.
- **Before/after:** `culprit bench --tag v1` and `--tag v2` on the same 6 scenarios. Metrics: culprit accuracy (x/6), hunk accuracy, fix verified (x/6), victim runs per bisect, cost per bisect, wall time. **Numbers are whatever the runs produce; nothing is estimated or rounded in our favour.**

**Instrumentation plan (apply at 12:30, from docs.neatlogs.com/sdk/python):**
- Install `pip install -U "neatlogs[anthropic]"` (Python ≥ 3.10, < 3.14). Key from `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` in `.env` (gitignored), never hardcoded. Default endpoint `https://ingest.neatlogs.com`.
- Two workflow names, one per entry point: `culprit-bisect` (Culprit CLI `run`/`resume`/`bench`) and `refunddesk-support-agent` (each victim task run, launched as a subprocess in a worktree).
- Capture Anthropic calls with **one** mechanism only: `neatlogs.wrap(Anthropic())` (the docs example uses OpenAI; Anthropic auto-detection is stated, not shown), or `instrumentations=["anthropic"]` with `init()` before the import. Never both.
- `@neatlogs.span(kind="WORKFLOW")` on each CLI command and on the victim's task entry point; `kind="TOOL"` on mock tools and on Culprit's git/worktree/eval tools; `kind="AGENT"` on Selector/Localiser/Fixer.
- Per-run metadata via `wrap()` kwargs (`commit_sha`, `task_id`, `repetition`, `run_id`), which become `neatlogs.workflow.<key>`. This is inferred from the docs, so verify in the dashboard.
- Both entry points are one-shot processes, so call `neatlogs.flush()` then `neatlogs.shutdown()` at exit (in `finally`).
- Open: the docs don't show how to read the current trace ID. Ask on Discord or use the CLI/Public API to look traces up by `run_id`/`task_id` metadata.

### 14.2 Entire
- Both repos (`piedpiper-neathacks` = Culprit, `refunddesk` = victim) connected via the Entire GitHub App; `entire enable` in each.
- **Product use:** Culprit reads the culprit commit's session context (`entire checkpoint explain <sha>`) to recover intent.
- **Build use:** every meaningful commit of Culprit is checkpointed; the checkpoint for the v1 → v2 fix is the headline evidence (Sessions → Changes).
- **Trails** (if access granted): the v1 → v2 fix done as a Trail. **Graph** optional.
- Submission includes checkpoint link `https://entire.io/gh/OWNER/REPO/commit/FULL_SHA` and checkpoint ID.

### 14.3 cfo.ai
- **Input:** `culprit export-costs` → Google Sheet (cfo.ai lists Google Sheets as a data connection; fall back to manual upload/entry if the import doesn't work).
- **Measured actuals:** cost per victim run, victim runs per bisect, Culprit LLM cost per bisect, wall time.
- **Pricing scenarios to model** (hypotheses, not facts):
  - **A. Flat SaaS:** $49 / $199 per repo/month with a bisect quota.
  - **B. Customer's own model key + platform fee** (recommended hypothesis): customer pays victim-run LLM cost; we charge a platform fee.
  - **C. Metered:** platform fee + per-bisect charge.
- **Questions for Ari:** gross margin per customer under A vs B at 10/50/200 bisects/month · break-even repos with 2 founders · runway under base/upside/downside acquisition · stress test with a 10× more expensive victim agent.
- **Deliverable:** exported business plan (pricing, costs, revenue, runway) in `/business/` and linked from the README.

## 15. Success metrics

| Metric | Target for submission |
|---|---|
| Culprit accuracy on R1–R6 | Reported for v1 and v2 (aim: v2 ≥ v1 and ≥ 5/6) |
| Fix verified on R1 | Required for the demo |
| Recovery shown | ≥ 1 skip and ≥ 1 resample in a recorded run |
| Cost per bisect | Measured and within the per-bisect budget cap |
| Evidence complete | All mandatory submission items in §4 present |

Targets are aims, not claims. The README reports actual values only.

## 16. Building in public (drafts, not published)
1. **"Our bisect agent blamed the wrong commit 2/6 times. Here's the trace that showed why."** (use whatever v1 actually scored)
2. **15-second clip:** a midpoint commit fails to install → SKIP → neighbour tested → bisect continues; a 3/5 result → INCONCLUSIVE → resampled.
3. **Before/after card:** v1 vs v2 benchmark table + Entire checkpoint link of the fixing session + "one bisect costs us $__" from the cfo.ai model.

## 17. Demo video (≤ 3:00)

## 9. Victim agent and seeded benchmark

### 9.1 Victim agent: "RefundDesk"
A customer-support agent that resolves refund requests using **mock tools** backed by a local JSON store:
`lookup_order`, `get_refund_policy`, `issue_refund`, `escalate_to_human`, `send_customer_email`.
The mock layer can inject failures (timeouts, `status: failed` payloads) deterministically per task seed.

**Eval suite:** 20 tasks + 6 held-out tasks. Each task = customer message + initial store state + **deterministic checker** on the final store state and tool-call log (e.g. "refund issued exactly once for ≤ $500", "escalated when order not found", "no refund when lookup failed").

### 9.2 Seeded regressions (ground truth)
Each scenario is a commit range of ~12–16 commits in the separate victim repo, with noise commits (docs, refactors, logging) around one culprit.

| ID | Culprit change | Intended gain | Symptom |
|---|---|---|---|
| **R1 (hero)** | "Make it faster": coding agent parallelises tool calls and **removes tool-result validation** | Lower latency | Refunds issued when `lookup_order` failed |
| R2 | Prompt cleanup drops the "> $500 needs escalation" rule | Shorter prompt / cost | Large refunds issued without escalation |
| R3 | Tool schema renames `order_id` → `id` without updating the description | API consistency | Wrong/missing arguments on lookup |
| R4 | `max_retries` 3 → 0 "to reduce latency" | Latency | Fails on flaky-tool tasks |
| R5 | Conversation history window shortened | Token cost | Loses customer details from earlier turns |
| R6 | Lenient JSON parsing of tool calls | Fewer parse errors | Malformed calls executed with defaults |

Plus **one uninstallable commit** (broken dependency pin) placed near the midpoint of at least two scenarios, to exercise skip recovery.

**Honesty rule:** The regressions are deliberately seeded. R1 is created through a real coding-agent session (captured by Entire) given the instruction "make it faster". We say this plainly in the demo and README.

## 10. Verification

A fix is **verified** only if all hold:
1. **Quality:** On full suite + held-out tasks × k, the Wilson interval for `bad+fix` overlaps or exceeds the `good` baseline interval.
2. **Intended gain kept:** The intent metric (latency / tokens / cost, taken from the commit intent) for `bad+fix` is no worse than `bad` by more than a configured tolerance.
3. **No new failures:** No task that passes on `good` fails consistently (all k) on `bad+fix`.

**Benchmark verification of Culprit itself** (`culprit bench`): for each of R1–R6, record whether the culprit commit was correct, whether the hunk was correct, whether the fix verified, victim runs used, cost, wall time. Ground truth is stored in `bench/ground_truth.json` in the Culprit repo (never in the victim repo). Victim history branches use neutral names (`hist/a`…`hist/f`); the scenario mapping lives only in the Culprit repo.

- **Moment worth screenshotting:** the fake-victim log, `hunk ranking (llm): h4, h3, h1`, then `localise:h4: 1/15 … → BAD`, then `localise:h3: 14/15 … → GOOD`, then `responsible: hunk 3 (refunddesk/agent.py:3)`.

- **Done: M5 part 2, the Fixer and Verifier (PRD §8.4, §10), as `culprit fix <run_id>`** (fake victim only, $0). Shared run loading moved into `finished.py`, so `localise` and `fix` don't touch the orchestrator.
  - **Fixer:** one AI call per attempt returns the intended gain (latency/tokens/cost/none) and exact search-and-replace edits. Culprit builds the patch itself, and only the responsible hunks' files may change.
  - **Verifier:** runs the full suite plus held-out tasks × k at the bad head with the patch applied. It passes only if quality is restored, the intended gain is kept (10% tolerance) and there are no new always-failing tasks. Failed attempts are fed back; after 2, the responsible hunks' revert is verified instead.
  - **Fake-victim log** (the culprit also made the agent faster):
    - `fix:1: 34/36 … latency 300 vs bad 100; FAILED: intended gain lost`
    - `fix:2: 34/36 … latency 100 vs bad 100; VERIFIED`
    - With no model, both attempts fail and the hunk revert is `verified_revert`.
  - 109 tests pass (13 new).

The "no task that always passed now always fails" gate is what catches such a fix. A Fisher test, like the regression gate's, would be stricter; candidate for M4.
- **Moment worth screenshotting:** the two `fix:` lines above: the Verifier refusing a fix that quietly gives the speed-up back.

  - **Staged baseline** (`culprit/baseline.py`): every task ×1 on both ends, then the full k only on tasks that didn't pass on both. Both ends run the same (task, repetition) set, and the Fisher gate uses the runs actually made.
  - **Baseline reuse** (`culprit/reuse.py`): results at a commit are copied from an earlier run with the same commit SHA, suite SHA, victim provider and model, eval module and k. Each copied row records its source (`task_runs.reused_from_run` / `reused_from_id`, plus the `baseline_reuse` artifact) and isn't counted as spend again.

# Blockers, unsupported features and known discrepancies

Each entry lists what the PRD assumed, what the tool actually supports (sources in `docs/research.md`), and the fallback we chose.

## Known discrepancies

### neatlogs cost for `claude-sonnet-5-5` differs from the list price

- **Observed:** for one call of 131 input and 18 output tokens, neatlogs reported `costUsd = 0.000663` (trace `ffdf497989747bf30856935f187e6013`, LLM span). That matches $3/$15 per MTok.
- **List price:** Anthropic's published list price for `claude-sonnet-5-5` is $2/$10 per MTok (cached 2026-10-06), which gives $0.000442 for the same call.
- **Decision:** Culprit's ledger (`culprit.llm.ANTHROPIC_PRICES`, $2/$10) is the only source of truth for cost, `export-costs` and cfo.ai. neatlogs' cost fields are not used in any cost number. Evidence tables that show neatlogs costs label them "neatlogs-reported, not used".

## Unsupported or changed vs the PRD

| PRD assumption | Reality | Fallback |
|---|---|---|
| Look up victim traces by `run_id` / `commit_sha` metadata (§14.1) | The read API and CLI can't filter on, or return, custom span attributes | Culprit stores every trace ID in the ledger. Its own traces use `session_id = run_id`, and run context also goes into each span's input JSON so readback can verify it |
| Read the current trace ID in code (§14.1 open question) | No getter in the SDK | `inject_trace_context()` W3C traceparent; verified to equal the read API's `traceId` |
| Investigate on v1 benchmark runs (§14.1) | Dashboard only; no API or CLI | Use Investigate by hand in the dashboard; record findings and screenshots in `evidence/` |
| Detection "`status: failed` followed by `issue_refund`" (§14.1) | Detections are per-span regex or conditional rules; a cross-span sequence can't be expressed in one rule | Not built yet (M4). Plan: regex on `issue_refund` tool spans plus a Culprit-side sequence check |
| `entire checkpoint explain` intent | The `## Intent` field can be a harness event (`<task-notification>`) or `*(no prompt recorded)*`, and `--json` carries no intent | Culprit reads the session's typed prompts from `--transcript` when Intent is a placeholder; commit message and diff when there is no checkpoint |
| OpenRouter provider | Dropped at first, then reinstated as the fallback (Sat evening) | Anthropic (Sonnet 5.5) when `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is set, otherwise OpenRouter (GLM 5.3). Culprit picks the victim model once per run and records it, so all commits are judged by the same model |
## Known limitations and next steps

- Built: M1–M3, M5 (`culprit localise`, `culprit fix`) and M6 (`culprit report`, `export-costs`), plus v2 staged and reused baselines. Not done yet: localise and fix on the real victim, the real v1 vs v2 benchmark, and neatlogs Investigate/Detections. v2's real-victim savings are projected, not measured.

## Submission

Requirements confirmed from https://neatlogs.com/hackathon (read 2026-10-10):

- [ ] Uses neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai (cfo.ai business plan covering pricing, costs, revenue, runway)
- [ ] Before/after run of the agent with compared numbers (e.g., two neatlogs traces)
- [ ] neatlogs trace links or screenshots
- [ ] Entire checkpoints or entire-graph output
- [ ] A run where an action failed, showing what the agent did next
- [ ] Building-in-public links tagged #neatHack
- [ ] Public repo with commits dated during the hackathon
- [ ] Demo video (the length limit isn't on the page; the PRD says ≤ 3 min, *pending confirmation*)
- [ ] Submit on X by quoting the official neatlogs post with team, name, project, public repo and demo. Window: Mon 12 Oct 2026, 7:00–11:55 PM IST

Judging weights (published): agent 30%, use of neatlogs/Entire/cfo.ai 25%, demo video 20%, building in public 15%, usefulness/originality 10%.

# Culprit

**`git bisect` for agent behaviour, with receipts.**

Give Culprit a good ref, a bad ref and an eval suite. It finds the commit that made your LLM agent
worse, even though evals are noisy and some commits won't install. It then reads *why* that change was
made from the coding-agent session recorded by Entire. Every step is traced in neatlogs and recorded in
a ledger, so each verdict can be audited.

Team PiedPiper, neatHack 2026. Build log: [`hackathon.md`](hackathon.md). Full technical guide:
[`HOW_IT_WORKS.md`](HOW_IT_WORKS.md). Spec: [`PRD.md`](PRD.md). Demo script: [`DEMO.md`](DEMO.md).

## The problem

Agent quality can degrade quietly over many commits: a prompt tweak here, a "make it faster" refactor
there, often written by a coding agent. Finding the commit responsible is hard for three reasons:

- **Evals are noisy.** The same commit can pass a task once and fail it the next time, so plain
  `git bisect` with one run per commit can blame the wrong commit.
- **Old commits break.** A bad dependency pin in the middle of the range stops a naive bisect.
- **Nobody remembers why.** Reverting the culprit also throws away whatever it was meant to improve.

## What Culprit does

1. **Pins the eval suite.** One snapshot of the suite judges every commit in the range, and the ledger
   records its SHA.
2. **Checks there is something to find.** It measures both ends, and a one-sided Fisher exact test
   (p < 0.05) must say good really beats bad. Otherwise it stops with `no_regression` rather than hunt
   for noise.
3. **Bisects with statistics.** Each step runs the tasks that dropped from good to bad, k times each.
   A 95% Wilson interval wholly above or below the threshold decides GOOD or BAD; if it straddles,
   Culprit resamples, and it flags any verdict it had to guess (`low_confidence`).
4. **Skips what won't install.** A commit that fails `uv sync --locked` is SKIPped and a neighbour is
   tested, as `git bisect skip` does.
5. **Explains the culprit.** It reads the commit's Entire checkpoint for the intent, passed through a
   leakage filter, and falls back to the commit message and diff when there is no checkpoint.
6. **Localises and fixes** (`culprit localise`, `culprit fix`). It finds the responsible hunk(s) by
   reverting them, writes a minimal fix, and verifies it on the full and held-out suites. The fix must
   keep the intended gain. These have been tested on the fixture victim only; see
   [Limitations](#limitations).
7. **Reports.** `culprit report <run_id>` writes markdown and static HTML. `culprit export-costs`
   writes per-run cost, victim runs and wall time as CSV for the business model.

Infrastructure failures (429, 5xx, timeouts) are retried and never counted against a commit. Budget
caps stop a run with the best current range. `culprit resume` continues any stopped run without
redoing finished work.

## Results so far (benchmark v1, real victim)

Six planted-bug branches of RefundDesk (see [the honesty note](#honesty-note-the-bugs-are-planted)).
Victim model GLM 5.3 via OpenRouter, k = 3, 26-task suite pinned at RefundDesk `main` `ba86ed0`.
Sources: [`evidence/bench-v1.md`](evidence/bench-v1.md), [`evidence/RUNS.md`](evidence/RUNS.md).

| Branch | Outcome | Found | Bad baseline | Victim runs | Cost | Run | Culprit trace (neatlogs) |
|---|---|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| `hist/a` | correct `no_regression` | – | 78/78 | 156 | $0.37 | `c35e241d27e0` | `851077c16289680e6bf3b7b07455eacc` |
| `hist/b` (hero) | **correct** | `397c427` | 57/78 | 240 | $0.60 | `ff50e3620fdd` | `d80e61a81918c7eb3ffd917a2509efb0` |
| `hist/c` | **correct** | `acf3b7d` | 72/78 | 180 | $0.43 | `61e567f792c4` | `ed3c0d768895933ef77599ed58694410` |
| `hist/d` | correct `no_regression` | – | 78/78 | 156 | $0.34 | `bc1019babecf` | `2dd7899a4c406576e022d25907315b6f` |
| `hist/e` | correct `no_regression` | – | 78/78 | 156 | $0.33 | `07ef56df395f` | `cf641747c092456c11249b1847391589` |
| `hist/f` | **correct** | `1777d44` | 51/78 | 252 | $0.61 | `2a355484b100` | `22cf8fbf2da34aa1eadc1d66517f33b5` |

- **Accuracy: 6/6 scored correct.** That breaks down as all **3 visible** planted bugs found exactly,
  plus 3 correct `no_regression` results on bugs that an independent check showed the suite can't see
  (next section).
- **Total:** 1,140 victim runs, 0 infrastructure errors, $2.70, 49m 27s of run time (bench-v1 totals
  from the ledger). The good end was 78/78 in every run.
- **Recovery on the real victim:** `hist/b` and `hist/f` SKIPped their uninstallable commit (`22a37db`,
  `2ad118e`) on the first bisect step and still landed on the planted commit. No step on the real victim
  needed resampling. The resample path is shown on the fixture victim instead.
- **The gate mattered:** on `hist/c`, 78/78 vs 72/78 have overlapping 95% intervals, so our original
  "intervals don't overlap" gate would have said `no_regression`. The Fisher gate gave p = 0.014 and
  the bisect found `acf3b7d`.
- **Every Culprit trace passed `culprit verify-trace`** (one root, no orphans, run ID and commit SHA on
  every span).

Not measured yet: hunk accuracy and fix verification on the real victim, and the v2 benchmark. See
[Limitations](#limitations).

### v1 → v2: cheaper baselines

Measuring both ends was the most expensive part of every run: 156 of `hist/b`'s 240 victim runs. v2
makes it cheaper in two ways:

- **Staged baseline.** Every task runs ×1 on both ends, and only tasks that didn't pass on both get the
  full k. Both ends run the same set, and the Fisher gate counts the runs actually made.
- **Baseline reuse.** Results at a commit are copied from an earlier run with the same commit SHA,
  suite SHA, victim model and k. Each copied row records the run it came from and isn't counted as
  spend again.

On the fixture victim, over 4 scenarios: **510 victim runs (v1) → 430 (v2) → 335 (v2, good end reused)
→ 270 (v2, both ends reused)**. Every run found the planted commit, and bisect runs were unchanged
([`evidence/v2-efficiency-fixture.md`](evidence/v2-efficiency-fixture.md)).

TODO: the v2 benchmark on the real victim (`evidence/bench-v2.md`). Its numbers will replace this
fixture-only comparison.

## Setup

You need Python ≥ 3.12, [`uv`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), git, and (for intent) the
[Entire CLI](https://docs.entire.io) (we used 0.11.4).

Clone both repos side by side:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/rahilmavani/piedpiper-neathacks.git              # Culprit
git clone https://github.com/rahilmavani/piedpiper-neathacks-refunddesk.git   # RefundDesk, the victim
cd piedpiper-neathacks && uv sync
```

Culprit only ever creates worktrees of the victim under `.culprit/worktrees/`. It never edits your
victim checkout. If the victim isn't at `../refunddesk`, set `CULPRIT_VICTIM_REPO` or pass `--repo`.

Create a `.env` in **each** repo. Both are gitignored, and RefundDesk's needs the same model key:

```bash
NEATLOGS_API_KEY=...        # tracing (optional; without it tracing is off)
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=...       # if set: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (claude-sonnet-5-5)
OPENROUTER_API_KEY=...      # otherwise: GLM 5.3 (z-ai/glm-5.3) via OpenRouter
# optional overrides, which must belong to the selected provider:
# VICTIM_MODEL=...  CULPRIT_MODEL=...
```

The provider is chosen from the keys present: Anthropic first, then OpenRouter. A run records its
victim provider and model, and passes them to every commit, so all commits are judged by the same
model. All published numbers were measured on GLM 5.3.

## How to run

```bash
set -a; source .env; set +a
uv run pytest -q                       # free: no model calls, tracing off

# Free demo on a generated fake victim (no LLM)
uv run python tests/fixtures/make_victim.py /tmp/victim --commits 14 --breaks-at 10 --unbuildable-at 7 --noisy-from 9 --noisy-pass 0.6
uv run culprit run --repo /tmp/victim --good good-v1.0 --bad main

# Real victim (costs money: about $0.60 on GLM 5.3 for hist/b)
uv run culprit run --repo ../piedpiper-neathacks-refunddesk --good good-v1.0 --bad origin/hist/b --budget-usd 5
uv run culprit resume <run_id> [--budget-usd 6]     # continue a stopped run
uv run culprit localise <run_id>                    # responsible hunk(s)
uv run culprit fix <run_id>                         # minimal fix + verification
uv run culprit report <run_id>                      # .culprit/reports/report-<run_id>.{md,html}
uv run culprit verify-trace <run_id>                # audit the run's neatlogs traces
uv run culprit bench --tag v1 --score-latest        # score runs against bench/ground_truth.json
uv run culprit export-costs --format csv --out business/runs.csv
```

`culprit run --no-reuse --no-staged` reproduces v1's baseline behaviour.

## How the three tools are used

### neatlogs

- **Culprit is traced.** Each run is one trace in workflow `culprit`, with the neatlogs session ID set
  to the run ID. Git, worktree, install, victim runs, decisions and Entire calls are spans, and each span
  carries the run ID and commit SHA.
- **The victim is traced.** Every RefundDesk task run is its own trace (workflow `refunddesk-eval`),
  tagged with Culprit's run ID, commit, task and repetition, so each data point in a bisect links to
  the agent run behind it.
- **Readback audit.** `culprit verify-trace <run_id>` pulls a run back through the neatlogs CLI and
  checks it against the trace contract. All six v1 runs pass (167–284 spans each).
- **A finding:** neatlogs prices `claude-sonnet-5-5` at $3/$15 per MTok against the $2/$10 list price.
  Culprit's own price table is the only cost source
  ([`evidence/neatlogs-cost-discrepancy.md`](evidence/neatlogs-cost-discrepancy.md),
  [`BLOCKERS.md`](BLOCKERS.md)).
- TODO: Investigate and Detections on the v1 runs (dashboard only; see `BLOCKERS.md`).

### Entire

- **In the product:** for the culprit commit, Culprit runs `entire checkpoint explain <sha>` in the
  victim repo and takes the Intent. When the Intent is a placeholder, it uses the session's typed
  prompts from `--transcript`. When there is no checkpoint, it uses the commit message and diff. Only
  the examined commit's checkpoint is read, and a leakage filter strips anything that could reveal the
  benchmark answers.
- **In the build:** both repos have Entire enabled, so Culprit's own commits and every planted-bug
  commit in RefundDesk carry `Entire-Checkpoint` trailers.
- In run `ff50e3620fdd` the intent fell back to the commit message and diff, because the Entire CLI
  wasn't installed on the machine that ran it. TODO: the hero commit's intent read through Entire on
  a recorded run.

### cfo.ai

- [`business/cfo-inputs.md`](business/cfo-inputs.md) holds measured unit costs from the ledger and
  three pricing scenarios, all labelled hypotheses: (A) flat per-repo subscription, (B) bring your own
  model key plus a platform fee, and (C) metered per bisect.
- `culprit export-costs --format csv` produces the per-run inputs.
- TODO: the cfo.ai business plan (pricing, costs, revenue, runway), exported to `business/`.

## Honesty note: the bugs are planted

RefundDesk and its six bugs were built by us, on purpose, so that Culprit's answers can be checked
against a known truth (PRD §9.2).

- **How they were made.** Each planted commit was **explicitly requested** from a Claude Code session
  in the RefundDesk repo, with a realistic reason (speed, cost, consistency), and Entire recorded those
  sessions. The hero bug on `hist/b` came from a session told to make RefundDesk faster by running
  tool calls in parallel and dropping per-result validation. That session first measured the code and
  pushed back. We told it to proceed.
- **Answers are kept out of reach.** Branch names are neutral (`hist/a`…`hist/f`). The answer key
  lives only in this repo ([`bench/ground_truth.json`](bench/ground_truth.json)), and Culprit never
  feeds this repo's files to a model.
- **Three of the six bugs turned out invisible to the suite**, which we didn't plan. On `hist/a`, `d`
  and `e`, Culprit's baselines gave 78/78 at the bad head and the gate said `no_regression`. A clean
  result could also mean Culprit missed something, so we didn't take Culprit's word for it. A separate
  strength check ([`bench/strength.md`](bench/strength.md)) ran the full 26-task suite at seeds 3–5,
  which no Culprit baseline uses, on `good-v1.0` and each bad head: **78/78 on all four**, one-sided
  Fisher p = 1.00, 312 runs, $0.711, 0 errors. The raw per-run results are in
  [`evidence/strength-check-glm.jsonl`](evidence/strength-check-glm.jsonl). Reading the code explains
  why:
  - **a:** the `order_id` → `id` rename is consistent across schema, agent, checker and tests.
  - **d:** the shortened prompt kept the over-$500 rule, and a code guard blocks such refunds anyway.
  - **e:** lenient argument defaults only fire when the model omits an argument, and GLM 5.3 never did.

  The benchmark scores a `no_regression` as correct only when such an independent measurement exists.
  Otherwise it's `no_regression_unverified`. So the honest headline is **3 of 3 visible bugs found,
  and 3 correct "nothing to find" results**.
- **The hero bug's visibility was also measured independently:** on the 6 harder retry tasks × 3 seeds,
  `good-v1.0` passed 18/18 and the hero commit `397c427` passed 0/18.

## Limitations

- **Localise and fix are unproven on the real victim.** They have been tested on the fixture only.
  TODO: `culprit localise` / `culprit fix` on `hist/b`.
- **The v2 savings are measured on the fixture only.** The real-victim v2 benchmark isn't done yet.
  The fixture has 5 of 10 tasks sensitive to the planted bug, against 7 of 26 on RefundDesk.
- **The staged baseline can miss a task.** A task that dropped from good to bad but happened to pass
  its single screen run on the bad end gets no further runs. The other dropped tasks still carry the
  signal.
- **One model, one suite.** All published runs used GLM 5.3. Only the hero bug's visibility is
  measured on Claude Sonnet 5.5. A bug the suite can't see is reported as `no_regression`; Culprit
  can't find what the evals don't measure.
- **Task selection is a plain ranking.** It ranks tasks by pass-rate drop. The planned
  neatlogs-trace-based selection isn't built.
- **Budget overshoot.** The budget is checked per batch, so a run can overshoot its cap by up to one
  batch of victim runs (4 by default).
- **The leakage filter is deliberately broad.** It drops harmless lines containing words like "seed".
- **Wall time includes pauses.** It runs from start to finish in the ledger, so it includes any pause
  before a resume.

## Repo map

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `src/culprit/` | The product: `orchestrator.py` (run loop), `bisect.py`, `stats.py`, `baseline.py` + `reuse.py` (v2), `localise.py`, `fix.py`, `bench.py`, `report.py`, `costs.py`, `entire.py`, `tracing.py` / `readback.py`, `ledger.py` |
| `tests/` | Unit and end-to-end tests on a generated fake victim (`tests/fixtures/make_victim.py`); no model calls, tracing off |
| `bench/` | Scenarios, ground truth, strength checks |
| `evidence/` | Run register, benchmark results, raw check data |
| `business/` | cfo.ai inputs |
| `scripts/` | Strength check, v1 vs v2 fixture comparison, trace helpers |

2. **Checks there is something to find.** It measures both ends, and a one-sided Fisher exact test
   (p < 0.05) must say good really beats bad. Otherwise it stops with `no_regression` rather than hunt
   for noise.
3. **Bisects with statistics.** Each step runs the tasks that dropped from good to bad, k times each.
   A 95% Wilson interval wholly above or below the threshold decides GOOD or BAD; if it straddles,
   Culprit resamples, and it flags any verdict it had to guess (`low_confidence`).
4. **Skips what won't install.** A commit that fails `uv sync --locked` is SKIPped and a neighbour is
   tested, as `git bisect skip` does.
5. **Explains the culprit.** It reads the commit's Entire checkpoint for the intent, passed through a
   leakage filter, and falls back to the commit message and diff when there is no checkpoint.
6. **Localises and fixes** (`culprit localise`, `culprit fix`). It finds the responsible hunk(s) by
   reverting them, writes a minimal fix, and verifies it on the full and held-out suites. The fix must
   keep the intended gain. These have been tested on the fixture victim only; see
   [Limitations](#limitations).
7. **Reports.** `culprit report <run_id>` writes markdown and static HTML. `culprit export-costs`
   writes per-run cost, victim runs and wall time as CSV for the business model.

Infrastructure failures (429, 5xx, timeouts) are retried and never counted against a commit. Budget
caps stop a run with the best current range. `culprit resume` continues any stopped run without
redoing finished work.

## Results so far (benchmark v1, real victim)

Six planted-bug branches of RefundDesk (see [the honesty note](#honesty-note-the-bugs-are-planted)).
Victim model GLM 5.3 via OpenRouter, k = 3, 26-task suite pinned at RefundDesk `main` `ba86ed0`.
Sources: [`evidence/bench-v1.md`](evidence/bench-v1.md), [`evidence/RUNS.md`](evidence/RUNS.md).

| Branch | Outcome | Found | Bad baseline | Victim runs | Cost | Run | Culprit trace (neatlogs) |

| `hist/b` (hero) | **correct** | `397c427` | 57/78 | 240 | $0.60 | `ff50e3620fdd` | `d80e61a81918c7eb3ffd917a2509efb0` |
| `hist/c` | **correct** | `acf3b7d` | 72/78 | 180 | $0.43 | `61e567f792c4` | `ed3c0d768895933ef77599ed58694410` |

  plus 3 correct `no_regression` results on bugs that an independent check showed the suite can't see
  (next section).
- **Total:** 1,140 victim runs, 0 infrastructure errors, $2.70, 49m 27s of run time (bench-v1 totals
  from the ledger). The good end was 78/78 in every run.
- **Recovery on the real victim:** `hist/b` and `hist/f` SKIPped their uninstallable commit (`22a37db`,
  `2ad118e`) on the first bisect step and still landed on the planted commit. No step on the real victim
  needed resampling. The resample path is shown on the fixture victim instead.

  "intervals don't overlap" gate would have said `no_regression`. The Fisher gate gave p = 0.014 and
  the bisect found `acf3b7d`.

  every span).

[Limitations](#limitations).

makes it cheaper in two ways:

- **Staged baseline.** Every task runs ×1 on both ends, and only tasks that didn't pass on both get the
  full k. Both ends run the same set, and the Fisher gate counts the runs actually made.
- **Baseline reuse.** Results at a commit are copied from an earlier run with the same commit SHA,
  suite SHA, victim model and k. Each copied row records the run it came from and isn't counted as
  spend again.

On the fixture victim, over 4 scenarios: **510 victim runs (v1) → 430 (v2) → 335 (v2, good end reused)
→ 270 (v2, both ends reused)**. Every run found the planted commit, and bisect runs were unchanged
([`evidence/v2-efficiency-fixture.md`](evidence/v2-efficiency-fixture.md)).

TODO: the v2 benchmark on the real victim (`evidence/bench-v2.md`). Its numbers will replace this
fixture-only comparison.

## Setup

You need Python ≥ 3.12, [`uv`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), git, and (for intent) the
[Entire CLI](https://docs.entire.io) (we used 0.11.4).

Clone both repos side by side:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/rahilmavani/piedpiper-neathacks.git              # Culprit
git clone https://github.com/rahilmavani/piedpiper-neathacks-refunddesk.git   # RefundDesk, the victim
cd piedpiper-neathacks && uv sync
```

Culprit only ever creates worktrees of the victim under `.culprit/worktrees/`. It never edits your
victim checkout. If the victim isn't at `../refunddesk`, set `CULPRIT_VICTIM_REPO` or pass `--repo`.

Create a `.env` in **each** repo. Both are gitignored, and RefundDesk's needs the same model key:

```bash
NEATLOGS_API_KEY=...        # tracing (optional; without it tracing is off)
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=...       # if set: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (claude-sonnet-5-5)
OPENROUTER_API_KEY=...      # otherwise: GLM 5.3 (z-ai/glm-5.3) via OpenRouter
# optional overrides, which must belong to the selected provider:
# VICTIM_MODEL=...  CULPRIT_MODEL=...
```

The provider is chosen from the keys present: Anthropic first, then OpenRouter. A run records its
victim provider and model, and passes them to every commit, so all commits are judged by the same
model. All published numbers were measured on GLM 5.3.

## How to run

```bash
set -a; source .env; set +a
uv run pytest -q                       # free: no model calls, tracing off

# Free demo on a generated fake victim (no LLM)
uv run python tests/fixtures/make_victim.py /tmp/victim --commits 14 --breaks-at 10 --unbuildable-at 7 --noisy-from 9 --noisy-pass 0.6
uv run culprit run --repo /tmp/victim --good good-v1.0 --bad main

# Real victim (costs money: about $0.60 on GLM 5.3 for hist/b)
uv run culprit run --repo ../piedpiper-neathacks-refunddesk --good good-v1.0 --bad origin/hist/b --budget-usd 5
uv run culprit resume <run_id> [--budget-usd 6]     # continue a stopped run
uv run culprit localise <run_id>                    # responsible hunk(s)
uv run culprit fix <run_id>                         # minimal fix + verification
uv run culprit report <run_id>                      # .culprit/reports/report-<run_id>.{md,html}
uv run culprit verify-trace <run_id>                # audit the run's neatlogs traces
uv run culprit bench --tag v1 --score-latest        # score runs against bench/ground_truth.json
uv run culprit export-costs --format csv --out business/runs.csv
```

`culprit run --no-reuse --no-staged` reproduces v1's baseline behaviour.

### neatlogs

- **Culprit is traced.** Each run is one trace in workflow `culprit`, with the neatlogs session ID set
  to the run ID. Git, worktree, install, victim runs, decisions and Entire calls are spans, and each span
  carries the run ID and commit SHA.
- **The victim is traced.** Every RefundDesk task run is its own trace (workflow `refunddesk-eval`),
  tagged with Culprit's run ID, commit, task and repetition, so each data point in a bisect links to
  the agent run behind it.
- **Readback audit.** `culprit verify-trace <run_id>` pulls a run back through the neatlogs CLI and
  checks it against the trace contract. All six v1 runs pass (167–284 spans each).
- **A finding:** neatlogs prices `claude-sonnet-5-5` at $3/$15 per MTok against the $2/$10 list price.
  Culprit's own price table is the only cost source
  ([`evidence/neatlogs-cost-discrepancy.md`](evidence/neatlogs-cost-discrepancy.md),
  [`BLOCKERS.md`](BLOCKERS.md)).
- TODO: Investigate and Detections on the v1 runs (dashboard only; see `BLOCKERS.md`).

### Entire

- **In the product:** for the culprit commit, Culprit runs `entire checkpoint explain <sha>` in the
  victim repo and takes the Intent. When the Intent is a placeholder, it uses the session's typed
  prompts from `--transcript`. When there is no checkpoint, it uses the commit message and diff. Only
  the examined commit's checkpoint is read, and a leakage filter strips anything that could reveal the
  benchmark answers.
- **In the build:** both repos have Entire enabled, so Culprit's own commits and every planted-bug
  commit in RefundDesk carry `Entire-Checkpoint` trailers.
- In run `ff50e3620fdd` the intent fell back to the commit message and diff, because the Entire CLI
  wasn't installed on the machine that ran it. TODO: the hero commit's intent read through Entire on
  a recorded run.

### cfo.ai

- [`business/cfo-inputs.md`](business/cfo-inputs.md) holds measured unit costs from the ledger and
  three pricing scenarios, all labelled hypotheses: (A) flat per-repo subscription, (B) bring your own
  model key plus a platform fee, and (C) metered per bisect.
- `culprit export-costs --format csv` produces the per-run inputs.
- TODO: the cfo.ai business plan (pricing, costs, revenue, runway), exported to `business/`.

## Honesty note: the bugs are planted

RefundDesk and its six bugs were built by us, on purpose, so that Culprit's answers can be checked
against a known truth (PRD §9.2).

- **How they were made.** Each planted commit was **explicitly requested** from a Claude Code session
  in the RefundDesk repo, with a realistic reason (speed, cost, consistency), and Entire recorded those
  sessions. The hero bug on `hist/b` came from a session told to make RefundDesk faster by running
  tool calls in parallel and dropping per-result validation. That session first measured the code and
  pushed back. We told it to proceed.
- **Answers are kept out of reach.** Branch names are neutral (`hist/a`…`hist/f`). The answer key
  lives only in this repo ([`bench/ground_truth.json`](bench/ground_truth.json)), and Culprit never
  feeds this repo's files to a model.
- **Three of the six bugs turned out invisible to the suite**, which we didn't plan. On `hist/a`, `d`
  and `e`, Culprit's baselines gave 78/78 at the bad head and the gate said `no_regression`. A clean
  result could also mean Culprit missed something, so we didn't take Culprit's word for it. A separate
  strength check ([`bench/strength.md`](bench/strength.md)) ran the full 26-task suite at seeds 3–5,
  which no Culprit baseline uses, on `good-v1.0` and each bad head: **78/78 on all four**, one-sided
  Fisher p = 1.00, 312 runs, $0.711, 0 errors. The raw per-run results are in
  [`evidence/strength-check-glm.jsonl`](evidence/strength-check-glm.jsonl). Reading the code explains
  why:
  - **a:** the `order_id` → `id` rename is consistent across schema, agent, checker and tests.
  - **d:** the shortened prompt kept the over-$500 rule, and a code guard blocks such refunds anyway.
  - **e:** lenient argument defaults only fire when the model omits an argument, and GLM 5.3 never did.

  The benchmark scores a `no_regression` as correct only when such an independent measurement exists.
  Otherwise it's `no_regression_unverified`. So the honest headline is **3 of 3 visible bugs found,
  and 3 correct "nothing to find" results**.
- **The hero bug's visibility was also measured independently:** on the 6 harder retry tasks × 3 seeds,
  `good-v1.0` passed 18/18 and the hero commit `397c427` passed 0/18.

## Limitations

- **Localise and fix are unproven on the real victim.** They have been tested on the fixture only.
  TODO: `culprit localise` / `culprit fix` on `hist/b`.
- **The v2 savings are measured on the fixture only.** The real-victim v2 benchmark isn't done yet.
  The fixture has 5 of 10 tasks sensitive to the planted bug, against 7 of 26 on RefundDesk.
- **The staged baseline can miss a task.** A task that dropped from good to bad but happened to pass
  its single screen run on the bad end gets no further runs. The other dropped tasks still carry the
  signal.
- **One model, one suite.** All published runs used GLM 5.3. Only the hero bug's visibility is
  measured on Claude Sonnet 5.5. A bug the suite can't see is reported as `no_regression`; Culprit
  can't find what the evals don't measure.
- **Task selection is a plain ranking.** It ranks tasks by pass-rate drop. The planned
  neatlogs-trace-based selection isn't built.
- **Budget overshoot.** The budget is checked per batch, so a run can overshoot its cap by up to one
  batch of victim runs (4 by default).
- **The leakage filter is deliberately broad.** It drops harmless lines containing words like "seed".
- **Wall time includes pauses.** It runs from start to finish in the ledger, so it includes any pause
  before a resume.

## Repo map

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `src/culprit/` | The product: `orchestrator.py` (run loop), `bisect.py`, `stats.py`, `baseline.py` + `reuse.py` (v2), `localise.py`, `fix.py`, `bench.py`, `report.py`, `costs.py`, `entire.py`, `tracing.py` / `readback.py`, `ledger.py` |
| `tests/` | Unit and end-to-end tests on a generated fake victim (`tests/fixtures/make_victim.py`); no model calls, tracing off |
| `bench/` | Scenarios, ground truth, strength checks |
| `evidence/` | Run register, benchmark results, raw check data |
| `business/` | cfo.ai inputs |
| `scripts/` | Strength check, v1 vs v2 fixture comparison, trace helpers |

Give Culprit a good ref, a bad ref and an eval suite. It finds the commit that made your LLM agent
worse, even though evals are noisy and some commits won't install. It then reads *why* that change was
made from the coding-agent session recorded by Entire. Every step is traced in neatlogs and recorded in
a ledger, so each verdict can be audited.

[`HOW_IT_WORKS.md`](HOW_IT_WORKS.md). Spec: [`PRD.md`](PRD.md). Demo script: [`DEMO.md`](DEMO.md).

## The problem

Agent quality can degrade quietly over many commits: a prompt tweak here, a "make it faster" refactor
there, often written by a coding agent. Finding the commit responsible is hard for three reasons:

- **Evals are noisy.** The same commit can pass a task once and fail it the next time, so plain
  `git bisect` with one run per commit can blame the wrong commit.
- **Old commits break.** A bad dependency pin in the middle of the range stops a naive bisect.
- **Nobody remembers why.** Reverting the culprit also throws away whatever it was meant to improve.

## What Culprit does

1. **Pins the eval suite.** One snapshot of the suite judges every commit in the range, and the ledger
   records its SHA.
2. **Checks there is something to find.** It measures both ends, and a one-sided Fisher exact test
   (p < 0.05) must say good really beats bad. Otherwise it stops with `no_regression` rather than hunt
   for noise.
3. **Bisects with statistics.** Each step runs the tasks that dropped from good to bad, k times each.
   A 95% Wilson interval wholly above or below the threshold decides GOOD or BAD; if it straddles,
   Culprit resamples, and it flags any verdict it had to guess (`low_confidence`).
4. **Skips what won't install.** A commit that fails `uv sync --locked` is SKIPped and a neighbour is
   tested, as `git bisect skip` does.
5. **Explains the culprit.** It reads the commit's Entire checkpoint for the intent, passed through a
   leakage filter, and falls back to the commit message and diff when there is no checkpoint.
6. **Localises and fixes** (`culprit localise`, `culprit fix`). It finds the responsible hunk(s) by
   reverting them, writes a minimal fix, and verifies it on the full and held-out suites. The fix must
   keep the intended gain. These have been tested on the fixture victim only; see
   [Limitations](#limitations).
7. **Reports.** `culprit report <run_id>` writes markdown and static HTML. `culprit export-costs`
   writes per-run cost, victim runs and wall time as CSV for the business model.

Infrastructure failures (429, 5xx, timeouts) are retried and never counted against a commit. Budget
caps stop a run with the best current range. `culprit resume` continues any stopped run without
redoing finished work.

[`HOW_IT_WORKS.md`](HOW_IT_WORKS.md). Spec: [`PRD.md`](PRD.md). Demo script: [`DEMO.md`](DEMO.md).

## The problem

Agent quality can degrade quietly over many commits: a prompt tweak here, a "make it faster" refactor
there, often written by a coding agent. Finding the commit responsible is hard for three reasons:

- **Evals are noisy.** The same commit can pass a task once and fail it the next time, so plain
  `git bisect` with one run per commit can blame the wrong commit.
- **Old commits break.** A bad dependency pin in the middle of the range stops a naive bisect.
- **Nobody remembers why.** Reverting the culprit also throws away whatever it was meant to improve.

## What Culprit does

1. **Pins the eval suite.** One snapshot of the suite judges every commit in the range, and the ledger
   records its SHA.
2. **Checks there is something to find.** It measures both ends, and a one-sided Fisher exact test
   (p < 0.05) must say good really beats bad. Otherwise it stops with `no_regression` rather than hunt
   for noise.
3. **Bisects with statistics.** Each step runs the tasks that dropped from good to bad, k times each.
   A 95% Wilson interval wholly above or below the threshold decides GOOD or BAD; if it straddles,
   Culprit resamples, and it flags any verdict it had to guess (`low_confidence`).
4. **Skips what won't install.** A commit that fails `uv sync --locked` is SKIPped and a neighbour is
   tested, as `git bisect skip` does.
5. **Explains the culprit.** It reads the commit's Entire checkpoint for the intent, passed through a
   leakage filter, and falls back to the commit message and diff when there is no checkpoint.
6. **Localises and fixes** (`culprit localise`, `culprit fix`). It finds the responsible hunk(s) by
   reverting them, writes a minimal fix, and verifies it on the full and held-out suites. The fix must
   keep the intended gain. These have been tested on the fixture victim only; see
   [Limitations](#limitations).
7. **Reports.** `culprit report <run_id>` writes markdown and static HTML. `culprit export-costs`
   writes per-run cost, victim runs and wall time as CSV for the business model.

Infrastructure failures (429, 5xx, timeouts) are retried and never counted against a commit. Budget
caps stop a run with the best current range. `culprit resume` continues any stopped run without
redoing finished work.

Sources: [`evidence/bench-v1.md`](evidence/bench-v1.md), [`evidence/RUNS.md`](evidence/RUNS.md).

### v1 → v2: cheaper baselines

Measuring both ends was the most expensive part of every run: 156 of `hist/b`'s 240 victim runs. v2
makes it cheaper in two ways:

  full k. Both ends run the same set, and the Fisher gate counts the runs actually made.
- **Baseline reuse.** Results at a commit are copied from an earlier run with the same commit SHA,
  suite SHA, victim model and k. Each copied row records the run it came from and isn't counted as
  spend again.

## Setup

You need Python ≥ 3.12, [`uv`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), git, and (for intent) the
[Entire CLI](https://docs.entire.io) (we used 0.11.4).

Clone both repos side by side:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/rahilmavani/piedpiper-neathacks.git              # Culprit
git clone https://github.com/rahilmavani/piedpiper-neathacks-refunddesk.git   # RefundDesk, the victim
cd piedpiper-neathacks && uv sync
```

Culprit only ever creates worktrees of the victim under `.culprit/worktrees/`. It never edits your
victim checkout. If the victim isn't at `../refunddesk`, set `CULPRIT_VICTIM_REPO` or pass `--repo`.

Create a `.env` in **each** repo. Both are gitignored, and RefundDesk's needs the same model key:

```bash
NEATLOGS_API_KEY=...        # tracing (optional; without it tracing is off)
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=...       # if set: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (claude-sonnet-5-5)
OPENROUTER_API_KEY=...      # otherwise: GLM 5.3 (z-ai/glm-5.3) via OpenRouter
# optional overrides, which must belong to the selected provider:
# VICTIM_MODEL=...  CULPRIT_MODEL=...
```

The provider is chosen from the keys present: Anthropic first, then OpenRouter. A run records its
victim provider and model, and passes them to every commit, so all commits are judged by the same
model. All published numbers were measured on GLM 5.3.

## How to run

```bash
set -a; source .env; set +a
uv run pytest -q                       # free: no model calls, tracing off

# Free demo on a generated fake victim (no LLM)
uv run python tests/fixtures/make_victim.py /tmp/victim --commits 14 --breaks-at 10 --unbuildable-at 7 --noisy-from 9 --noisy-pass 0.6
uv run culprit run --repo /tmp/victim --good good-v1.0 --bad main

# Real victim (costs money: hist/b cost $0.60 on GLM 5.3)
uv run culprit run --repo ../piedpiper-neathacks-refunddesk --good good-v1.0 --bad origin/hist/b --budget-usd 5
uv run culprit resume <run_id> [--budget-usd 6]     # continue a stopped run
uv run culprit localise <run_id>                    # responsible hunk(s)
uv run culprit fix <run_id>                         # minimal fix + verification
uv run culprit report <run_id>                      # .culprit/reports/report-<run_id>.{md,html}
uv run culprit verify-trace <run_id>                # audit the run's neatlogs traces
uv run culprit bench --tag v1 --score-latest        # score runs against bench/ground_truth.json
uv run culprit export-costs --format csv --out business/runs.csv
```

`culprit run --no-reuse --no-staged` reproduces v1's baseline behaviour.

## How the three tools are used

### neatlogs

- **Culprit is traced.** Each run is one trace in workflow `culprit`, with the neatlogs session ID set
  to the run ID. Git, worktree, install, victim runs, decisions and Entire calls are spans, and each span
  carries the run ID and commit SHA.
- **The victim is traced.** Every RefundDesk task run is its own trace (workflow `refunddesk-eval`),
  tagged with Culprit's run ID, commit, task and repetition, so each data point in a bisect links to
  the agent run behind it.
- **Readback audit.** `culprit verify-trace <run_id>` pulls a run back through the neatlogs CLI and
  checks it against the trace contract. All six v1 runs pass (167–284 spans each).
- **A finding:** neatlogs prices `claude-sonnet-5-5` at $3/$15 per MTok against the $2/$10 list price.
  Culprit's own price table is the only cost source
  ([`evidence/neatlogs-cost-discrepancy.md`](evidence/neatlogs-cost-discrepancy.md),
  [`BLOCKERS.md`](BLOCKERS.md)).
- TODO: Investigate and Detections on the v1 runs (dashboard only; see `BLOCKERS.md`).

### Entire

- **In the product:** for the culprit commit, Culprit runs `entire checkpoint explain <sha>` in the
  victim repo and takes the Intent. When the Intent is a placeholder, it uses the session's typed
  prompts from `--transcript`. When there is no checkpoint, it uses the commit message and diff. Only
  the examined commit's checkpoint is read, and a leakage filter strips anything that could reveal the
  benchmark answers.
- **In the build:** both repos have Entire enabled, so Culprit's own commits and every planted-bug
  commit in RefundDesk carry `Entire-Checkpoint` trailers.
- In run `ff50e3620fdd` the intent fell back to the commit message and diff, because the Entire CLI
  wasn't installed on the machine that ran it. TODO: the hero commit's intent read through Entire on
  a recorded run.

### cfo.ai

- [`business/cfo-inputs.md`](business/cfo-inputs.md) holds measured unit costs from the ledger and
  three pricing scenarios, all labelled hypotheses: (A) flat per-repo subscription, (B) bring your own
  model key plus a platform fee, and (C) metered per bisect.
- `culprit export-costs --format csv` produces the per-run inputs.
- TODO: the cfo.ai business plan (pricing, costs, revenue, runway), exported to `business/`.

## Honesty note: the bugs are planted

RefundDesk and its six bugs were built by us, on purpose, so that Culprit's answers can be checked
against a known truth (PRD §9.2).

- **How they were made.** Each planted commit was **explicitly requested** from a Claude Code session
  in the RefundDesk repo, with a realistic reason (speed, cost, consistency), and Entire recorded those
  sessions. The hero bug on `hist/b` came from a session told to make RefundDesk faster by running
  tool calls in parallel and dropping per-result validation. That session first measured the code and
  pushed back. We told it to proceed.
- **Answers are kept out of reach.** Branch names are neutral (`hist/a`…`hist/f`). The answer key
  lives only in this repo ([`bench/ground_truth.json`](bench/ground_truth.json)), and Culprit never
  feeds this repo's files to a model.
- **Three of the six bugs turned out invisible to the suite**, which we didn't plan. On `hist/a`, `d`
  and `e`, Culprit's baselines gave 78/78 at the bad head and the gate said `no_regression`. A clean
  result could also mean Culprit missed something, so we didn't take Culprit's word for it. A separate
  strength check ([`bench/strength.md`](bench/strength.md)) ran the full 26-task suite at seeds 3–5,
  which no Culprit baseline uses, on `good-v1.0` and each bad head: **78/78 on all four**, one-sided
  Fisher p = 1.00, 312 runs, $0.711, 0 errors. The raw per-run results are in
  [`evidence/strength-check-glm.jsonl`](evidence/strength-check-glm.jsonl). Reading the code explains
  why:
  - **a:** the `order_id` → `id` rename is consistent across schema, agent, checker and tests.
  - **d:** the shortened prompt kept the over-$500 rule, and a code guard blocks such refunds anyway.
  - **e:** lenient argument defaults only fire when the model omits an argument, and GLM 5.3 never did.

  The benchmark scores a `no_regression` as correct only when such an independent measurement exists.
  Otherwise it's `no_regression_unverified`. So the honest headline is **3 of 3 visible bugs found,
  and 3 correct "nothing to find" results**.
- **The hero bug's visibility was also measured independently:** on the 6 harder retry tasks × 3 seeds,
  `good-v1.0` passed 18/18 and the hero commit `397c427` passed 0/18.

## Limitations

- **Localise and fix are unproven on the real victim.** They have been tested on the fixture only.
  TODO: `culprit localise` / `culprit fix` on `hist/b`.
- **The v2 savings are measured on the fixture only.** The real-victim v2 benchmark isn't done yet.
  The fixture has 5 of 10 tasks sensitive to the planted bug, against 7 of 26 on RefundDesk.
- **The staged baseline can miss a task.** A task that dropped from good to bad but happened to pass
  its single screen run on the bad end gets no further runs. The other dropped tasks still carry the
  signal.
- **One model, one suite.** All published runs used GLM 5.3. Only the hero bug's visibility is
  measured on Claude Sonnet 5.5. A bug the suite can't see is reported as `no_regression`; Culprit
  can't find what the evals don't measure.
- **Task selection is a plain ranking.** It ranks tasks by pass-rate drop. The planned
  neatlogs-trace-based selection isn't built.
- **Budget overshoot.** The budget is checked per batch, so a run can overshoot its cap by up to one
  batch of victim runs (4 by default).
- **The leakage filter is deliberately broad.** It drops harmless lines containing words like "seed".
- **Wall time includes pauses.** It runs from start to finish in the ledger, so it includes any pause
  before a resume.

+  model key plus a platform fee, and (C) metered per bisect.
+- `culprit export-costs --format csv` produces the per-run inputs.
+- TODO: the cfo.ai business plan (pricing, costs, revenue, runway), exported to `business/`.
+## Honesty note: the bugs are planted
+RefundDesk and its six bugs were built by us, on purpose, so that Culprit's answers can be checked
+against a known truth (PRD §9.2).
+- **How they were made.** Each planted commit was **explicitly requested** from a Claude Code session
+  in the RefundDesk repo, with a realistic reason (speed, cost, consistency), and Entire recorded those
+  sessions. The hero bug on `hist/b` came from a session told to make RefundDesk faster by running
+  tool calls in parallel and dropping per-result validation. That session first measured the code and
+  pushed back. We told it to proceed.
+- **Answers are kept out of reach.** Branch names are neutral (`hist/a`…`hist/f`). The answer key
+  lives only in this repo ([`bench/ground_truth.json`](bench/ground_truth.json)), and Culprit never
+  feeds this repo's files to a model.
+- **Three of the six bugs turned out invisible to the suite**, which we didn't plan. On `hist/a`, `d`
+  and `e`, Culprit's baselines gave 78/78 at the bad head and the gate said `no_regression`. A clean
+  result could also mean Culprit missed something, so we didn't take Culprit's word for it. A separate
+  strength check ([`bench/strength.md`](bench/strength.md)) ran the full 26-task suite at seeds 3–5,
+  which no Culprit baseline uses, on `good-v1.0` and each bad head: **78/78 on all four**, one-sided
+  Fisher p = 1.00, 312 runs, $0.711, 0 errors. The raw per-run results are in
+  [`evidence/strength-check-glm.jsonl`](evidence/strength-check-glm.jsonl). Reading the code explains
+  why:
+  - **a:** the `order_id` → `id` rename is consistent across schema, agent, checker and tests.
+  - **d:** the shortened prompt kept the over-$500 rule, and a code guard blocks such refunds anyway.
+  - **e:** lenient argument defaults only fire when the model omits an argument, and GLM 5.3 never did.
+  The benchmark scores a `no_regression` as correct only when such an independent measurement exists.
+  Otherwise it's `no_regression_unverified`. So the honest headline is **3 of 3 visible bugs found,
+  and 3 correct "nothing to find" results**.
+- **The hero bug's visibility was also measured independently:** on the 6 harder retry tasks × 3 seeds,
+  `good-v1.0` passed 18/18 and the hero commit `397c427` passed 0/18.
+## Limitations
+- **Localise and fix are unproven on the real victim.** They have been tested on the fixture only.
+  TODO: `culprit localise` / `culprit fix` on `hist/b`.
+- **The v2 savings are measured on the fixture only.** The real-victim v2 benchmark isn't done yet.
+  The fixture has 5 of 10 tasks sensitive to the planted bug, against 7 of 26 on RefundDesk.
+- **The staged baseline can miss a task.** A task that dropped from good to bad but happened to pass
+  its single screen run on the bad end gets no further runs. The other dropped tasks still carry the
+  signal.
+- **One model, one suite.** All published runs used GLM 5.3. Only the hero bug's visibility is
+  measured on Claude Sonnet 5.5. A bug the suite can't see is reported as `no_regression`; Culprit
+  can't find what the evals don't measure.
+- **Task selection is a plain ranking.** It ranks tasks by pass-rate drop. The planned
+  neatlogs-trace-based selection isn't built.
+- **Budget overshoot.** The budget is checked per batch, so a run can overshoot its cap by up to one
+  batch of victim runs (4 by default).
+- **The leakage filter is deliberately broad.** It drops harmless lines containing words like "seed".
+- **Wall time includes pauses.** It runs from start to finish in the ledger, so it includes any pause
+  before a resume.
+## Repo map
+| Path | What |

+| `src/culprit/` | The product: `orchestrator.py` (run loop), `bisect.py`, `stats.py`, `baseline.py` + `reuse.py` (v2), `localise.py`, `fix.py`, `bench.py`, `report.py`, `costs.py`, `entire.py`, `tracing.py` / `readback.py`, `ledger.py` |
+| `tests/` | Unit and end-to-end tests on a generated fake victim (`tests/fixtures/make_victim.py`); no model calls, tracing off |
+| `bench/` | Scenarios, ground truth, strength checks |
+| `evidence/` | Run register, benchmark results, raw check data |
+| `business/` | cfo.ai inputs |
+| `docs/` | `research.md` (what the neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai docs support), `neatlogs.md` (tracing contract and readback) |
+| `scripts/` | Strength check, v1 vs v2 fixture comparison, trace helpers |
